findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple chemical sanitizers to not meet required chemical sanitizing concentrations:
1) The dish machine at the bar (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- sanitizer was replaced, machine was primed, and ran until it was observed to be in compliance.
2) The sanitizer bucket was observed at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the bucket was remade to 200 ppm.
Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine, and 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a gallon of milk held past it’s expiration date (6/9/26). CORRECTED- the milk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure prepackaged foods are not held past their expiration or “best by” dates to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets along the 3 door refrigerator to be frayed. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained in proper repair. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink at the bar to only dispense cold water- the hot water faucet was nonoperational. All sinks designated for hand washing should be able to reach a minimum temperature of 85F. Inspector will return on 02/24/25 to check for compliance.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contact an accumulation of debris:
1) The soda nozzle at the bar banquet room
2) 2 ladles handing in ready to use position with an accumulation of food debris on the food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- items were moved to the dish machine for ware washing. 
3) The water fountain in the hallway contains a significant amount of limescale and biofilm.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods. Inspector will return on 02/24 to check that line items 1 and 3 have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.  [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple pieces of equipment to be in disrepair:
1) The gaskets along the 3 door refrigerator are frayed.
2) The hinges along the pizza prep cooler are not holding the lid in place.
Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained in proper repair. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in need of physical repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The hand-sink at the (main) bar should be sealed to the wall.
2) FIRST REPEAT: Coving on the West wall of the dry food storage is peeling.
3) FIRST REPEAT: Coving on the wall directly to the right of the entryway of the chemical storage room. Coving is also peeling on the North side behind the water heater.
4) Coving in the Southwest corner of the dry storage is absent.
Items that cannot be moved easily for cleaning should be adhered to the wall. Seal items to wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple cell phones stored on the prep counter of the kitchen. Ensure personal belongings are kept in a designated area, separate from food and nonfood contact surfaces used to serve food to the public to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the coffee dispenser in the kitchen to contain a significant amount of residue around the water outlet. CORRECTED- the outlet was wiped with a clean sanitizer rag. Ensure all food-contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed wet sanitizer rags at the bottom of the reach in cooler at the bar in the banquet room. Education occurred with the person in charge. If clean sanitizer rags are being used to hold condensation, they should be changed everyday.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(A) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills from TABLEWARE and carry-out containers that occur as FOOD is being served shall be: (1) Maintained dry; and (2) Used for no other purpose. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in need of physical repair;
1) The hand-sink at the (main) bar is loose.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine in the kitchen has turned black and appears fragmented.
3) Coving on the West wall of the dry food storage had began peeling off.
4) Coving on the wall directly to the right of the entryway of the chemical storage room. Coving is also peeling on the North side behind the water heater.
Items that cannot be moved easily for cleaning should be adhered to the wall. Seal items to wall to prevent degradation of physical facilities.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soils.
1. The heat lamp was observed to have an accumulation of soil coating.
2. The grill and fryers was observed to have an accumulation of soil and grease underneath and on the sides.

The person in charge (PIC) was made aware of the soil accumulation in the areas mentioned. PIC said that cleaning schedule will increase in frequency from biweekly to weekly. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned frequently enough to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a personal backpack hanging at the drying rack opposite of the dish machine in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge moved the backpack to the designated storage area in the chemical room. Ensure personal belongings are kept in a designated area, separate from food and nonfood contact surfaces used to serve food to the public to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Liquid egg and raw pork were observed to be stored above cabbage and potatoes. The egg had spilled onto the vegetables. CORRECTED- Discussed with the Person In Charge (PIC) who voluntarily discarded the vegetables. The storage order was rearranged to the appropriate standard, with raw proteins below vegetables and ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that food items are stored properly to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1)(a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed. [P]

findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: The baffle of the ice machine was observed to have accumulated pink and black molds. Discussed with PIC, who said that they will have the machine cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are routinely monitored, cleaned, and always in adequate state to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

Ensure that all sanitizer buckets and solution meets the appropriate concentration as instructed by the label. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
A blue container with white powder (appeared to be flour) was observed in the dry storage. Discussed with PIC and the labeling of the substance was corrected. Ensure that all items such as white powders that are not easily identifiable are labeled properly.

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soils.
1. The floor drain area of the banquet room bar was observed to have an accumulation of soil.
2. The floor drain on the cookline, near the prep sink, was observed to have an accumulation of soil on the floor and the plumbing.
3. The heat lamp was observed to have an accumulation of soil coating.
4. The grill and fryers was observed to have an accumulation of soil and grease underneath and on the sides. 
5. The drain area of the tea machine station was observed to have an accumulation of slime mold.
PIC was made aware of the soil accumulation in the areas mentioned. PIC said that cleaning was schedule to happen soon. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned frequently enough to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Bar soda nozzle on the west end and in the banquet hall bar observed with mold accumulation. Nozzles are cleaned weekly, but this does not appear to be sufficient. Increase cleaning frequency. Maintain soda nozzles clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED- Soda nozzles were cleaned during this inspection. (Previously observed at the 12/15/23 and 3/14/24 inspections.)
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket at the bar observed with no measurable quat concentration. CORRECTED- PIC refilled buckets after letting the wall-mounted sanitizer dispenser run a little longer. Sanitizer observed at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer is made to proper concentration. Educate employees on using test strips to verify sanitizer concentration when preparing sanitizer buckets.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400ppm. [P]
